newsitem.title: UK: NCL BUYS CRUISESHIP AIDA FOR $180 MLN.
newsitem.headline: NCL BUYS CRUISESHIP AIDA FOR $180 MLN.

text.p: NCL Holding ASA, the Norwegian cruise shipping company, said its has entered into a purchase and charter-back agreement for the 1,186-berth cruiseship Aida.
NCL said it on Tuesday entered into an agreement to buy Aida for $180 million from Deutsche Seetouristik GmbH, and charter it back to the German company for a year at a cost of $27 million.
The charter will start from October 24, the planned delivery date. NCL said the purchase is linked to a currency adjustment clause that could allow for the gross price to be reduced by $2.9 million.
NCL said it intends to form a co-operation agreement with Arkona Reisen, a travel company linked to Deutsche Seetouristik. The German cruise company controls a second cruise vessel, Arkona.
The deal will strengthen NCL's position in the fast-growing European cruise market, NCL president and chief executive Geir Aune said in a statement.
Mr Aune said: "The company intends to enter into a closer co-operation with Arkona Reisen in Germany with regard to sale and marketing of the vessel in Europe."
"The parties will enter into discussions about if and how to organise co-operation. If final agreement is reached, the ship will continue to operate under the existing concept."
A spokeswoman for Deutsche Seetouristik declined to comment. "I am afraid we have nothing to say at this time."
Aida was built at Kvaerner Masa-Yards in Finland and delivered to Deutsche Seetouristik last summer. -- Reuters Shipping News +44 171 542 4087/4012. Fax 5017.
